entry.title:
Some observations about the "total" automation of software engineering:
1. There are more software ...
entry.summary: Continuing the conversation from yesterday's Social posts, Francois Chollet argues that despite agents now writing roughly 100% of code, software engineering has not been 'totally automated': there are more engineers than in 2025, they work harder than ever, and company bottom lines are not improving from AI adoption. He concludes that automation must be analyzed at the systems level, since automating one aspect simply shifts bottlenecks and creates new friction elsewhere.

entry.title: we’re getting used to it by now but DeepSeek calling this a “minor update” while moving Terminal-Ben...
entry.summary: Thom Wolf highlights that DeepSeek labeled an update minor while jumping Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 31.2 to 42.3, reporting 77.0 on DeepSWE versus 74.0 for Opus 5 and 73.0 for GPT-5.6 Sol, and notes faster task completion via shorter outputs as an underappreciated cost-curve lever, all under MIT-licensed weights; he asks how the numbers hold outside DeepSeek's own eval setup.

entry.title:
Can we predict electronic bands beyond DFT across different systems?
A material’s electronic band s...
entry.summary: Anima Anandkumar introduces O-krystal, a periodic E(3)-equivariant graph neural network that predicts electronic band structures beyond DFT by learning corrections to PBE calculations, evaluated across nearly 6,000 diverse 3D materials spanning metals, insulators, and magnetic systems.

entry.title: 🎉 Congrats @deepseek_ai on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017! Better scores and shorter outputs make it a gre...
entry.summary: vLLM congratulates DeepSeek on a new DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 checkpoint, noting better scores and shorter outputs suited to long agent loops. vLLM reports 1.3B tokens per dollar TCO on SemiAnalysis AgentX and 830K tok/s per GPU at 100 tok/s per user, with a claimed 5x agentic throughput improvement since day zero.

entry.title: There's something very odd going on with "distillation" if a cyber attack to steal api keys is loope...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert questions the collapsing of distinct phenomena under the label distillation: a cyber attack to steal API keys and model transfer stations to China are being looped together, and it is unclear why the volume is so high or how it relates to model training.

entry.title: This naming scheme is bonkers (minor model numbers and date tags) and the benchmark step is big. Cou...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert critiques a confusing new open-weight model naming scheme based on minor version numbers and date tags, but flags a large benchmark improvement, speculating the model could prove stronger than GLM 5.3 with built-in vision and asking if the king of open weights is back.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: OpenCode had a security breach last night related to a large scale distillation ...
entry.summary: MTSlive reports that OpenCode suffered a security breach overnight involving a large-scale model distillation attack affecting 1.4% of console users, with Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google collaborating on remediation.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 17, 2026
entry.summary:
Recursive AI development dominated discussion. Anthropic's Claude Devs reported Claude now writes ~90% of Claude Code with merged PRs doubling since June, and Boris Cherny credited Claude Code Review with catching nearly every bug — together signaling an AI self-improvement loop.

  • Policy and sovereignty ran hot: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch urged Europe not to cede frontier AI to the US and China (317k views); Anthropic reportedly drafted frontier-AI regulation with lawmakers; Nathan Lambert flagged China's signal on ending larger open models.
  • Open-source momentum: Jim Fan released the ASPIRE robotics framework; Perplexity open-sourced Decision Models; Artificial Analysis ranked Reflection's Beam among US open-weights leaders and crowned Liquid AI's d1-ultra on its Decision Index.
  • Hardware economics: vLLM's benchmark showing AMD MI355X beating NVIDIA B300 by 24% on Kimi K3 serving sparked infrastructure debate.

Overall sentiment: excitement about agentic and self-improving AI capabilities, mixed with growing policy anxiety in Europe, the US, and China.

entry.title:
Should Europe leave frontier AI to the Americans and the Chinese?
The idea has gained ground in Eur...
entry.summary: Arthur Mensch argues that the idea of Europe ceding frontier AI to the US and China, which is gaining ground in Europe, is a fundamental mistake, urging that Europe must build its own frontier capability while the choice remains open, linking to a full article.

entry.title:
Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's code.
From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account reports that roughly 90 percent of Claude Code's codebase is now written by Claude itself. From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled while the revert rate fell by over 40 percent, and the team published details on the code review process changes that enabled this.

entry.title: The back of the Navier-Stokes milestone shirt is the last line of the chain-of-thought from the solu...
entry.summary: Sam Altman shares that OpenAI commemorative merch for a Navier-Stokes milestone prints the final line of the chain-of-thought from the model's solution, confirming and celebrating a major mathematical reasoning achievement.

entry.title: I could not imagine being productive without Claude Code Review. It runs on all of my PRs, and catch...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social announcement, Cherny states Claude Code Review runs on all his pull requests and catches almost every bug before merging, calling it part of the secret sauce enabling his team to move fast while maintaining quality. Very high engagement: ~3,455 likes and 257k views.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Claude now writes about 90% of Claude Code’s code. From June to September, merge...
entry.summary: MTS Live shares a striking statistic that Claude now writes roughly 90% of Claude Code's own code, with merged PRs more than doubling from June to September while reverted PR share fell over 40%.

entry.title: We are open-sourcing V1.0 of our agentic robotics framework, ASPIRE, with full real robot skill disc...
entry.summary: Jim Fan announces open-sourcing V1.0 of ASPIRE, an agentic robotics framework with real-robot skill discovery and self-improvement. He reports that swapping the backend to OpenAI's Astra saturated their benchmarks to ~99% overnight, while Claude Opus 5.5 slightly edges out Astra on their robot simulation benchmark and Sonnet 5.5 hits a strong cost/capability Pareto point at $12/task. He frames Astra as a zero-to-one leap for robotics capability.

entry.title:
Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours.
Operating in a sandbox using on...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind reports that four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours, operating in a sandbox with only code and text. The agents wrote 2,783 programs, divided tasks via chat, shared notes, and debugged errors collaboratively without human help.

entry.title:
🚀 @AMD MI355X just showed competitive performance to NVIDIA B300 on @Kimi_Moonshot K3 serving!
8× M...
entry.summary: The vLLM project reports that 8x AMD MI355X beats NVIDIA HGX B300 by 24.4% throughput (7,567 vs 6,083 tok/s/GPU) at 50 tok/s/user serving Kimi K3 on the SemiAnalysis AgentX agentic coding benchmark, with 87.4% more tokens per dollar. The writeup covers the vLLM optimizations, AMD kernels, and hardware details that closed the gap, plus bottleneck-spotting patterns.

entry.title:
New from our STEM Fellows Program: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude.
Given pla...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces a result from its STEM Fellows Program: given plain-language instructions, Claude Mythos 5 designed quantum circuits that improve on the best published ones, sometimes by an order of magnitude or more, potentially accelerating quantum computing applications in chemistry and materials science.

entry.title: Reflection’s first model, Beam, scores 30 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's flagship evaluation of Reflection's Beam: scoring 30 on the Intelligence Index, second among US open-weights models behind Meta's Muse Spark Open (39) and ahead of NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (26); token-efficient at ~26K output tokens per task versus K2 Horizon's ~52K, strong on agentic workflows (48.5% AutomationBench-AA) but weaker in terminal tasks.

entry.title: Liquid AI has released d1-ultra, taking the #1 position on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces Liquid AI's release of d1-ultra, which tops the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1.0 with a score of 65, ahead of Jev 1.14 (57), GLiDE and Microsoft-Decision-1 (54). Priced at $0.042 per 1M input tokens (input-token-only billing), its gain is driven by a much lower hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience-Decision (85% non-hallucination vs 2% for d1), reflecting improved knowledge self-assessment.

entry.title: In a similar scramble I did to jump on AI in late 2022 (moving from remote work and nomads to AI app...
entry.summary: levelsio lays out a detailed strategy for chasing remaining moats as AI companies absorb other value: proprietary data (launching paid city-data and neighborhood-data APIs priced $2,490-$9,990/year), network effects (making his community nearly free to grow it), and audience/distribution pivots for his sites. Massive reach: ~256k views, 2,230 likes, 36 quotes.

pplx-decider-flash-v1.2: 4...
entry.summary: @AravSrinivas announces Perplexity has open-sourced two Decision Models: pplx-decider-flash-v1.2 (4B params, 1 cent per million tokens, top 4B model on the HF Decision Index) and pplx-decider-v1.2 (27B params, 2 cents per million tokens, #2 overall), available via the Perplexity Decisions API and as open weights on Hugging Face.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Anthropic has written a bill to regulate frontier AI and is meeting with lawmake...
entry.summary: MTSlive flags, per Politico, that Anthropic has drafted a bill to regulate frontier AI and is meeting with lawmakers about it.

entry.title: Notion AI lead @sarahmsachs explains why AI models have become 2–3x more capable in just a year, yet...
entry.summary: Sarah Sachs explores the gap between models that are 2-3x more capable year over year and knowledge workers who have not seen proportional productivity gains, framing it as a capability overhang caused by missing processes, products, and permissions, and advocating a context layer for agent-to-agent collaboration amid agent sprawl.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents have beaten Minecraft end-to-end in 27 hours and 14 m...
entry.summary: MTS Live reports that four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft end-to-end in 27 hours and 14 minutes without human help, coordinating through in-game chat, supporting teammates, and recovering items after deaths.

entry.title: Seems very important, as tons of people are tweeting about the end of bigger open models from China ...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert flags as very important a statement from China's MOCOM that many read as ending larger open models from China, noting the statement also intends to ease open-source technology via a near-automatic approval process whose implementation will be decisive.

entry.title:
Anthropic's @logangraham predicts AI will match the world's best hackers by early 2027:
Claude can ...
entry.summary: Graham predicts AI will match the world's best offensive hackers by end of 2026 to early 2027, saying Claude can already do things only ~1,000 people on Earth have done, and warns of proliferation into side-channel attacks, physics loopholes, and social engineering alongside defensive gains.

entry.title: This paper shows why I am skeptical of the idea that frontier models can be easily replaced by cheap...
entry.summary: Mollick expresses skepticism that frontier models can be easily replaced by cheaper alternatives, arguing that small accuracy and judgment advantages compound over long-horizon tasks, producing large gains in outcomes and error reduction.

entry.title: Penguin has moved up the publication date of my new book with Patchen Barss called "Smarter Than Us"...
entry.summary: Geoffrey Hinton announces that Penguin has moved up the publication date of his new book with Patchen Barss, Smarter Than Us, which explains how AI works for non-technical readers and discusses AI risks and what to do about them.

entry.summary: Cherny promotes Claude Slides as his new way to build slide decks, eliminating manual searching for assets like iPhone frame SVGs, with a call to try it and an attached demo. Very high engagement: over 3,000 likes and 214k views.

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL shares a new study showing frontier OpenAI models improved success rates on hard theory questions in math, physics, and economics from 3% to 35% over 16 months at roughly $15 per successful attempt, suggesting verification may be the new bottleneck.

entry.title:
Anthropic's @logangraham reveals the first proof-of-concept for self-replicating AI agents:

entry.summary: Logan Graham describes the first proof-of-concept of self-replicating AI agents, connecting it to the autonomous replication and adaptation threat model from early responsible scaling policies and warning that small, capable models could one day acquire their own compute.

entry.summary: Continuing our Social coverage of the Argon frontier story from earlier this week, Francois Chollet reports that Google Gemini-4-Argon shows a performance profile on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark similar to OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, declaring that Google has returned to the model frontier.

entry.title: We’ve committed to having evaluators assess our safety practices. We're in discussions with multiple...
entry.summary: Anthropic commits to external evaluation of its safety practices, announcing it has given employee-like access to a team from METR and is in discussions with multiple other organizations, with a post describing how it works with third-party evaluators.

entry.title: We want to support the mathematics community in turning progress in AI into deeper human understandi...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces a $5 million contribution to a new Simons Foundation initiative helping mathematicians examine, verify, and build on AI-produced results, including OpenAI's recently published results, with funding for workshops, conferences, model access, and compute for Simons-supported researchers.

entry.title: While sandboxes are a commodity, serving millions of them under production-grade traffic requires a ...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas announces Perplexity is open-sourcing SPACE, the sandbox platform that powers Perplexity Computer, arguing that serving millions of sandboxes under production-grade traffic requires significant engineering beyond commodity sandboxing.

entry.title: Neoclouds can't just lease GPUs. They need to own the full agent inference platform: open-weight mod...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas argues that neoclouds must move beyond GPU leasing to own the full agent inference stack: open-weight model serving (SGLang), fine-tuned models (Miles, River), and secure sandboxes (SPACE). He announces Perplexity looks forward to partnering with CoreWeave, Akamai, Crusoe, and others.

entry.title: Blue Rose Research's @davidshor reveals how belief that AI could threaten humanity's survival surged...
entry.summary: David Shor reports that belief AI could pose a serious threat to humanity's survival jumped from the 30s to 64% among voters in six months, calling it the birth of a new political issue comparable only to COVID in his career, and noting the public is still processing it in real time.

entry.summary: OpenAI announces GPT-Live-1.1, an update to Voice in ChatGPT, Codex, and dots adding new voices and improved accents in French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean, and Japanese, rolling out to all users with API access coming soon.

entry.title: Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now the leading US open weight model, scoring 26 on the Artificial...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Reddit release threads, Artificial Analysis's main announcement post covering the launch of Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (leading US open weight model, Intelligence Index 26, double its predecessor's score with ~60% fewer output tokens) and the new Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, with key takeaways on rankings, parameter efficiency, and NVFP4 quantization.

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert celebrates that US open-weight models are relevant again, noting that before this release US models lagged Chinese models dating back to February 2026, and estimates the new release cut that gap by at least half (roughly three months of progress).

entry.summary: Anthropic announces a $5 million commitment of funding, compute, and Claude access to support the mathematics community, managed by the Simons Foundation through workshops, conferences, and expert lectures to help mathematicians adapt to AI-driven change.

entry.title:
Introducing ExtractBenchPro: the most challenging benchmark for real-world document extraction.
We ...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) introduces ExtractBenchPro, a benchmark targeting the long tail of complex real-world document extraction (trial balances, well logs, loss runs) where frontier models saturate existing benchmarks; it tests document conventions, jargon density, and aggregation/reasoning.

entry.title:

entry.summary: Levelsio reports that data brokers are acquiring struggling SaaS datasets for $100K–$2M and reselling them to AI frontier labs so labs can absorb the SaaS functionality into their own apps, predicting where this trend leads.

entry.title: Blue Rose Research's @davidshor on why AI data centers have become a major issue in the midterms, wi...
entry.summary: Pollster David Shor explains that local opposition to AI data centers has exploded: only 12% of voters want one nearby versus 13% for a prison, down from the 40s eight months earlier, and both parties are running ads against data centers. He predicts AI will be the dominant political issue within a year.

entry.title: If it performs roughly what like the scores indicate, adoption of this model is going to go gangbust...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert predicts massive adoption for a new US open-weight model if its benchmark scores hold, calling it the first US open-weight model with near-frontier agentic capabilities, following the earlier step change from China's GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3.

entry.title: .@davidshor reveals how AI went from America's least important political issue to being ranked along...
entry.summary: David Shor describes polling showing AI rising from 40th of 40 voter priorities to 21st (tied with crime), with roughly half the increase since 2024 occurring over the two days of the media firestorm around the Coxon resignation.

GPT-6 Astra places first ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5; models remain roughly two orders of magnitude slower and pricier than humans.

entry.title: TPUs have different bottlenecks from GPUs: few cores so you don’t need yo think about parallelism as...
entry.summary: Tri Dao explains that TPUs differ from GPUs in bottleneck structure: fewer cores reduce parallelism concerns, large VMEM makes kernel fusion easier, but vector units have lower throughput so non-matmul operations need much more care.

entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account announces a major Claude Code desktop app update focused on running many sessions side by side, with faster session starts and better visibility into each session's activity.

entry.summary: Anthropic announces public beta support for OpenTelemetry tracing on the Claude Platform, covering the Messages API, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude SDKs, exportable to external observability stacks.

entry.summary: The anchor tweet of a DeepMind thread claiming Gemini 4 Argon is already driving scientific breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and protein design, with links to specific case studies.

entry.summary: Artificial Analysis adds DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to its AA-AgentPerf agentic inference benchmark, reporting NVIDIA GB300 leading with up to 261M tokens/s per MW at 100 tokens/s per user. The benchmark replays real agentic coding sessions with prompt caching and tool-call delays, and the leaderboard now features four models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.2/5.3.

entry.title: after switching our approach to building a "FirmOS", I'm increasingly confident that the future of a...
entry.summary: Yohei Nakajima (BabyAGI creator) argues the future of human-agent collaboration in organizations is a 'CompanyOS' — a continuously updated operating system storing rules, processes, decisions, and tooling rather than a monolithic 'company brain'. He frames it as a 'flipped playbook': instead of writing rules first (waterfall-style), the playbook evolves daily as the business learns, with source-of-truth data remaining in existing tools like CRMs.

entry.title: Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with Perplexity Computer. This u...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas describes a user case where Perplexity Computer took a Windows-only mechanical keyboard app with no documentation, decompiled the binary with headless Ghidra in its cloud sandbox, and rebuilt it as a native Rust app for Linux with music-synced lighting, 3D view, remapping, macros, and profiles.

entry.title: We’ve opened an office in Singapore—our fifth in the Asia-Pacific region. We’ve also signed an MOU w...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore and a memorandum of understanding with the Singaporean government covering AI safety and responsible adoption.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 14, 2026
entry.summary:
Demos and independent evaluations carried the freshest conversation.

entry.summary: Karpathy revives an earlier observation that public understanding of LLM capability is sharply stratified: roughly 6B people have barely touched LLMs, 1-2B are casual users who see them as improved search or writing aids, and only about 20M people (0.2%) use frontier-grade models professionally in math and code. He argues this perception gap is widening into a funnel rather than a simple disagreement between two camps.

entry.title: New paper from the team at Sakana AI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervisio...
entry.summary: Hardmaru (Sakana AI CEO) announces a new paper, MASS (Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision), which addresses the supervision bottleneck in open-ended AI research. The method has a single model organize copies of itself into structured multi-agent teams, alternately optimizing the team workflows and then fine-tuning (internalizing) successful coordination trajectories back into the base model, inspired by Minsky's Society of Mind.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 11, 2026
entry.summary:
Intelligence explosion skepticism dominated the day's discussion. Ramez Naam's interview thread series argued the AI self-improvement loop is 5-10x too weak for takeoff, citing OpenAI's own token/researcher figures, rapid plateaus when scaling Claude Opus 5.5 agent swarms, and gaps between Anthropic's system cards and leadership rhetoric.

  • Francois Chollet delivered the conceptual highlight: the field's shift from transductive token completion to inductive, on-the-fly reasoning-chain synthesis
  • Yann LeCun clarified his critique targets autoregressive discrete-token prediction specifically, not AI broadly
  • Nathan Lambert flagged low net data quality as a reward-hacking amplifier and reported a ~30% drop in top open-model HuggingFace downloads, prompting a metrics rebuttal from HF CEO Clement Delangue
  • Practitioner threads from Boris Cherny and LangChain's Harrison Chase emphasized orchestration efficiency: routing cut Open SWE costs 64%, and many agent steps are yes/no calls rather than generation
  • Naam showed intellectual honesty by self-rebutting on OpenAI's claimed math breakthrough, while Ethan Mollick captured the OpenAI-vs-Anthropic cultural moment via a mathematician's Opus 5.5 music video

Overall sentiment: empirically grounded and practitioner-focused, with the community favoring falsifiable claims over accelerationist hype.

He predicts major investment from frontier labs around open inference, open post-training, and real-world evals plus synthetic data methods, possibly built on open models.
